evals.prompt: Create a documentation screenshot that walks the reader through opening the WordPress editors from the admin bar. Use the pre-captured WordPress Playground screenshot at examples/sample-shot.webp (viewport 1440x900 CSS px, deviceScaleFactor 2) — do NOT capture a new screenshot. The bounding boxes of every relevant control are in evals/files/boxes.json (CSS px, screenshot top-left origin). Annotate the 'Edit Site' and 'Edit Page' admin-bar buttons so a reader knows to click them, framed with a browser chrome bar showing playground.wordpress.net. Deliver the rendered image and the config you authored into the outputs directory.
evals.expected_output: A .webp render in the established house style: both admin-bar buttons outlined, one tapered blue ribbon arrow arriving on each outline, chrome bar on top, no annotation collisions.
expectations: The render was produced by scripts/annotate.py from a config JSON, not by hand-drawn image code or a different drawing approach
The delivered image is a .webp whose final width is 1512 px (1440 css + 2*36 margin)
The config outlines the 'Edit Site' control using box [216, 0, 91, 32] from boxes.json (same values, plus a small padding setting), not eyeballed coordinates
The config outlines the 'Edit Page' control using box [424, 0, 98, 32] from boxes.json
Each outlined control has exactly one arrow, whose 'to' endpoint stops a few px (roughly 5-10) outside the outline edge rather than touching or entering the box
The two arrows do not cross each other (their horizontal spans do not overlap given both tails are below the targets)
The config includes chrome_bar with url playground.wordpress.net
Zoomed QA crops were generated (--crops) and the workflow shows the crops or full render were actually inspected before finishing

evals.prompt: Create an overview documentation image ('legend style') of the Playground Dock's main controls, using the pre-captured screenshot examples/sample-shot.webp (1440x900 CSS px, dsf 2) — do NOT capture a new screenshot. Bounding boxes are in evals/files/boxes.json. Document three controls with numbered callout cards: the refresh button (icon-only, circular control), the row of tool panes, and the Autosaved chip. The rest of the page should be visually de-emphasized while the Dock stays at full brightness. Deliver the rendered image and your config into the outputs directory.
evals.expected_output: A dimmed-overview render: three numbered white callout cards in one aligned row, each with a vertical arrow onto its outlined Dock control, Dock region undimmed.
expectations: The render uses the cards + outlines + dim mode of scripts/annotate.py (cards with target indexes, dim with a region)
The refresh button is outlined as a circle (type circle), not a rectangle
The dim region corresponds to the dock panel box [389, 766, 660, 126] (or a slightly padded version of it), keeping the Dock undimmed
Cards are ordered left-to-right to match the left-to-right order of their targets, so no card arrow crosses another
The render completed with no 'WARNING: text overflows card' message on stderr (card copy is short: 2-3 word titles, one short clause subtitles)
The delivered image is a .webp 1512 px wide

evals.prompt: A colleague left a half-finished annotation config at evals/files/broken-config.json for the screenshot examples/sample-shot.webp. First run scripts/annotate.py on it exactly as-is (from the skill root) and report precisely what happens. Then repair the config with the minimal set of fixes needed to render a sensible single-outline walkthrough image (the outline is the 'Edit Site' admin-bar button), and render it into the outputs directory. Report every problem the original config had.
evals.expected_output: An accurate report of the failure mode of the broken config (missing css_width, non-webp output, incomplete circle outline, invalid arrow axis, card target out of range, missing cards_top), plus a repaired config and a successful render.
expectations: The original config was actually executed and its failure honestly reported (not skipped or paraphrased from reading the config alone)
The report identifies at least these problems: missing css_width, output not ending in .webp, the empty circle outline, invalid arrow axis value, and the cards target index pointing outside outlines
The final workflow state is a successful render from a repaired config (exit 0), delivered as a .webp
The repaired config keeps the Edit Site rect outline [216, 0, 91, 32] and drops or fixes (rather than silently keeps) the broken circle, bad axis, and out-of-range card target
